examples.ko: 그 부대의 주둔은 삼 년 동안 계속됐어요.
examples.en: The unit's stationing there lasted three years.

examples.ko: 군인들의 주둔 때문에 마을이 조용하지 않아요.
examples.en: The village isn't quiet because of the soldiers stationed there.
The stationing period ended, so the unit came back.

examples.ko: 이 나라는 외국군의 주둔을 허락하지 않아요.
examples.en: This country does not allow foreign troops to be stationed here.
The soldiers' period of stationing is one year.
As the stationing dragged on, local residents also became uncomfortable.

explain: '주둔'은 뉴스나 역사 이야기에서 군대 이야기를 할 때 주로 나와요. 사람이 어느 곳에 잠깐 머무는 건 '머무르다'나 '묵다'라고 해요.
explain_en: 주둔 mostly shows up in news and history when talking about an army. For ordinary people staying somewhere for a while, Koreans say 머무르다 or 묵다.

examples.en: The army is stationed near the border.

examples.ko: 그 부대는 작년부터 이 도시에 주둔했어요.
examples.en: That unit has been stationed in this city since last year.
The soldiers will be stationed in the mountains.

examples.ko: 마을에 주둔하는 군인들이 시장에서 장을 봐요.
examples.en: The soldiers stationed in the village shop at the market.

examples.ko: 부대는 겨울 동안 여기에 주둔하고 있어요.
examples.en: The unit is stationed here for the winter.
People were worried because foreign troops were stationed there.

explain: 주어는 거의 군대나 부대예요. 장소 뒤에는 '에'를 붙여서 '국경에 주둔하다'라고 해요. 사람이 잠시 머무는 일에는 '머무르다'를 써요.
explain_en: The subject is almost always an army or a unit. Put 에 after the place, as in '국경에 주둔하다'. For a person staying somewhere briefly, use 머무르다.

examples.ko: 회사는 공장 증설을 올해 안에 끝낼 거예요.
examples.en: The company will finish expanding the factory this year.
The students were happy about the news that more buses would be added.

examples.ko: 증설 공사 때문에 길이 많이 막혀요.
examples.en: The roads are very congested because of the expansion work.

examples.ko: 병원은 병실 증설이 꼭 필요하다고 말했어요.
examples.en: The hospital said adding more patient rooms is absolutely necessary.

examples.ko: 서버 증설을 하고 나서 접속이 빨라졌어요.
examples.en: After the servers were added, connecting got faster.
The plan to add subway capacity was announced yesterday.

explain: '증설'은 공장·서버·병실처럼 이미 있는 시설에 더 붙일 때 써요. 처음 짓는 건 '건설'이나 '설립', 수나 양이 많아지는 건 '증가'라고 해요.
explain_en: 증설 is for adding more to a facility that already exists, such as a factory, server, or ward. Building something new is 건설 or 설립, and a plain rise in number or amount is 증가.

examples.en: The company is expanding with a new factory.
The school added two classrooms.

examples.ko: 다음 달에 버스 노선을 증설할 거예요.
examples.en: Next month they will add bus routes.

examples.ko: 서버를 증설하는 데 돈이 많이 들어요.
examples.en: It costs a lot of money to add servers.

examples.ko: 식당을 증설하고 나서 손님이 더 늘었어요.
examples.en: After the restaurant was expanded, more customers came.

examples.ko: 자리가 모자라서 좌석을 증설해서 쓰고 있어요.
examples.en: There weren't enough seats, so we added more and are using them.

explain: 목적어는 공장·서버·노선처럼 설비나 시설이에요. 사람 수나 가격을 늘릴 때는 '증설하다'가 아니라 '늘리다'나 '올리다'를 써요.
explain_en: The object is equipment or a facility, such as a factory, server, or route. For raising numbers of people or prices, use 늘리다 or 올리다 instead of 증설하다.

en: invite (an expert or teacher) to take a post or give a talk

examples.en: The school is bringing in a famous professor.
The university invited a teacher from abroad.
We will bring in a lecturer next semester.
I went to an event where an expert was invited to speak.
The church is looking to bring in a new pastor.

examples.ko: 회사가 디자이너를 초빙해서 새 제품을 만들었어요.
examples.en: The company brought in a designer and made a new product.

explain: '초빙하다'는 전문가나 선생님을 모셔 올 때 써요. 파티나 식사에 친구를 부를 때는 '초대하다'를 써야 자연스러워요. 친구에게 '초빙하다'라고 하면 어색해요.
explain_en: 초빙하다 is for bringing in an expert or a teacher. To invite a friend to a party or a meal, 초대하다 is the natural word, and 초빙하다 would sound odd.

examples.en: It rained a lot, so the road was flooded.
The underground parking lot flooded, so we moved the car.
They are bailing water out of the flooded house.

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 마을 전체가 침수될 뻔했어요.
examples.en: The whole village almost flooded because of the typhoon.

examples.ko: 우리 동네는 비가 오면 자주 침수돼요.
examples.en: My neighborhood often floods when it rains.

examples.ko: 집이 침수되고 나서 가구를 전부 버렸어요.
examples.en: After the house flooded, we threw out all the furniture.

explain: '침수되다'는 비나 홍수로 집·도로·차가 물에 잠길 때 써요. 사람이 물에 빠지는 일에는 쓰지 않고 '물에 빠지다'라고 해요. 일상 대화에서는 '잠기다'도 많이 들려요.
explain_en: 침수되다 is for houses, roads, or cars going under water after rain or a flood. It is not used for a person falling into water, where Koreans say 물에 빠지다. In daily talk you also hear 잠기다.

en: be in common use; be generally used; be accepted (in a place or group)

examples.en: This abbreviation is widely used on the internet.
In that country, dollars were accepted too.
I learned the greetings commonly used in Korea.

examples.ko: 이 방법은 다른 나라에서도 통용될 거예요.
examples.en: This method will be accepted in other countries too.

examples.ko: 그 말이 회사에서 통용돼서 저도 쓰기 시작했어요.
examples.en: That word was common at work, so I started using it too.
This card is accepted everywhere.

explain: '통용되다'는 말·돈·규칙이 어떤 장소나 집단에서 널리 받아들여질 때 써요. '사용되다'는 그냥 쓰인다는 뜻이고, '통용되다'는 거기서 통한다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 보통 '에서'와 같이 쓰여요.
explain_en: 통용되다 is for words, money, or rules that are widely accepted in a certain place or group. 사용되다 just means something is used, while 통용되다 adds the sense that it works there. It usually appears with 에서.

en: be desolate; be ruined; be run-down (land, town, or mind)

examples.en: After the war, the village became completely desolate.

examples.ko: 아무도 살지 않는 집이 황폐해 보여요.
examples.en: A house where no one lives looks run-down.
We planted trees again on the barren land.

examples.ko: 마음이 황폐할 때는 조용한 곳에서 쉬어요.
examples.en: When my heart feels worn out, I rest somewhere quiet.

examples.ko: 농사를 안 지어서 밭이 황폐하고 쓸쓸해요.
examples.en: No one farms it, so the field is ruined and lonely.
The city had fallen into ruin, so people left.

explain: '황폐하다'는 땅·마을·마음이 돌보는 사람 없이 거칠어졌을 때 써요. 그냥 오래된 건 '낡다'라고 하고, 사람 손이 떠나 망가진 느낌이면 '황폐하다'가 더 가까워요. '황폐해지다' 모양으로 많이 나와요.
explain_en: 황폐하다 is for land, towns, or a mind that has grown rough with no one caring for it. Something merely old is 낡다, while 황폐하다 fits when it looks ruined after people left. It often appears as 황폐해지다.

examples.en: In the movie, two men fight hand to hand in the street.

examples.ko: 어제 본 영화에서 두 사람이 오랫동안 격투했어요.
examples.en: In the movie I saw yesterday, two people fought for a long time.
In the movie, the hero will fight the villain.
I took a picture of them fighting.

examples.ko: 서로 붙잡고 격투하다가 둘 다 넘어졌어요.
examples.en: They grabbed each other, struggled, and both fell down.
Only after fighting for a good while did the two make up.

explain: '격투하다'는 맨몸으로 서로 치고받으며 싸울 때 써요. 말다툼은 '싸우다'나 '다투다'라고 하고, 운동 경기는 '시합하다'라고 해요. 일상에서는 '몸싸움하다'를 더 자주 들어요.
explain_en: 격투하다 is for fighting with bare hands, trading blows. A verbal quarrel is 싸우다 or 다투다, and a sports match is 시합하다. In daily talk 몸싸움하다 is heard more often.

examples.ko: 공룡 화석이 나와서 골격을 그대로 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: A dinosaur fossil was found, so we can see its whole skeleton.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 골격이 커서 어깨가 넓어요.
examples.en: That person has a large frame, so the shoulders are broad.
I saw a model of the human skeleton at the museum.

examples.ko: 글의 골격부터 먼저 짜고 내용을 채워요.
examples.en: I build the framework of the essay first and then fill in the content.

examples.ko: 아기의 골격은 아직 약해서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: A baby's bones are still weak, so you have to be careful.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 튼튼한 골격 위에 유리를 붙여서 지었어요.
examples.en: This building was made by attaching glass over a sturdy frame.

explain: '골격'은 뼈 전체의 짜임이나 몸의 큰 틀을 말해요. 뼈 하나하나는 '뼈'라고 하고, 몸집이나 몸매는 '체격'이라고 해요. 글이나 건물의 기본 구조를 '골격'이라고 하기도 해요.
explain_en: 골격 is the overall structure of the bones, or the body's basic frame. A single bone is 뼈, and one's physique is 체격. It is also used for the basic structure of a text or a building.

examples.ko: 학교 폭력 근절을 위해 선생님들이 모였어요.
examples.en: Teachers gathered to put an end to school violence.
Wiping out corruption is not easy.

examples.ko: 정부는 불법 주차 근절 방안을 발표했어요.
examples.en: The government announced measures to stamp out illegal parking.
Many citizens took part in the campaign to stamp it out.

examples.ko: 이 병은 백신 덕분에 근절에 가까워졌어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the vaccine, this disease is close to being wiped out.

examples.ko: 쓰레기 불법 투기 근절이 올해의 목표예요.
examples.en: Ending illegal dumping of trash is this year's goal.

explain: '근절'은 나쁜 일이나 병을 뿌리부터 없애는 일이에요. '폭력 근절', '부패 근절'처럼 나쁜 것과 같이 나와요. 좋은 일에는 쓰지 않고, 일상에서는 '없애다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: 근절 is about removing something bad or a disease at its root. It appears with bad things, as in '폭력 근절' and '부패 근절', never with good things. In everyday talk 없애다 is far more common.

examples.en: That disease has been wiped out in this region.
Violence is not easily stamped out.
I hope illegal ads get stamped out.

examples.ko: 범죄가 근절될 때까지 우리는 노력할 거예요.
examples.en: We will keep trying until crime is eliminated.

examples.ko: 오래된 나쁜 습관이 근절돼서 모두 기뻐했어요.
examples.en: The old bad habit was eliminated, and everyone was glad.

examples.ko: 사람이 걸리는 병 중에 완전히 근절된 병은 천연두뿐이에요.
examples.en: Smallpox is the only human disease that has been completely eradicated.

explain: '근절되다'는 누가 없앴는지보다 없어진 결과를 말해요. '근절되지 않다', '근절되기 어렵다'처럼 부정으로도 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 '없어지다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: 근절되다 focuses on the result of something disappearing, not on who removed it. It often appears in the negative, as in '근절되지 않다' and '근절되기 어렵다'. In daily talk 없어지다 is more common.

examples.en: The city is cracking down to end illegal parking.
The police promised to stamp out school violence.
The company will change only if bad practices are rooted out.

examples.ko: 이 병을 근절한 나라는 아직 없어요.
examples.en: No country has eradicated this disease yet.

examples.ko: 사기를 근절하고 싶으면 먼저 법을 지켜야 해요.
examples.en: If you want to stamp out fraud, you must first follow the law.

examples.ko: 시민들이 쓰레기 투기를 근절해서 거리가 깨끗해졌어요.
examples.en: Citizens put an end to illegal dumping, and the streets became clean.

explain: '근절하다'의 목적어는 폭력·부패·사기·병처럼 나쁜 것이에요. 뿌리까지 뽑는다는 느낌이라 계속 남아 있던 문제에 잘 어울려요. 가볍게 줄이는 일은 '줄이다'라고 해요.
explain_en: The object of 근절하다 is something bad, like violence, corruption, fraud, or a disease. It suits a problem that has stayed around for a long time. Merely reducing something is 줄이다.

en: be inherent; be immanent; exist within

examples.en: Possibility exists within every person.

examples.ko: 이 문제에는 더 큰 위험이 내재했어요.
examples.en: A bigger danger was hidden within this problem.
Try to find the meaning that lies within the work.
Responsibility will always be built into a choice.

examples.ko: 그 말에는 슬픔이 내재해서 듣기 힘들었어요.
examples.en: Sadness was hidden in those words, so it was hard to hear.

examples.ko: 겉으로 안 보여도 위험이 내재하고 있어요.
examples.en: Even if it doesn't show on the surface, danger lies within.

explain: '내재하다'는 논문이나 뉴스에서 주로 보이는 글말이에요. 말할 때는 '들어 있다', '담겨 있다'가 자연스러워요. 주어는 위험·가능성·의미처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것이에요.
explain_en: 내재하다 is bookish, seen mostly in papers and news. In speech, 들어 있다 and 담겨 있다 sound more natural. The subject is something unseen, such as danger, possibility, or meaning.

examples.en: Gas leaked out, so people went outside.
The company's information was leaked onto the internet.
The leaked oil spread into the sea.

examples.ko: 물이 누출될 수 있으니 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Water might leak out, so please check.
The pipes are old, so water keeps leaking out.

examples.ko: 시험 문제가 누출되고 나서 시험이 취소됐어요.
examples.en: After the exam questions leaked, the exam was canceled.

explain: '누출되다'는 가스·기름·물이 있어야 할 곳 밖으로 새어 나올 때 써요. 정보에는 '유출되다'를 더 자주 써요. 물이 새는 일상 상황은 '새다'가 가장 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 누출되다 is for gas, oil, or water escaping from where it should be. For information, 유출되다 is used more often. In everyday situations where water drips out, 새다 is the most natural.

examples.en: The factory leaked gas by mistake.
The old tank is leaking oil.
Who is the employee who leaked the information to the reporter?

examples.ko: 비밀을 누출하면 큰 벌을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you leak a secret, you can get a heavy penalty.

examples.ko: 배가 기름을 바다에 누출해서 문제가 생겼어요.
examples.en: The ship leaked oil into the sea and caused a problem.

examples.ko: 회사는 정보를 누출할 생각이 전혀 없었어요.
examples.en: The company had no intention at all of leaking the information.

explain: '누출하다'는 가스나 정보를 내보낸 쪽이 주어예요. 새어 나온 결과를 말할 때는 '누출되다'가 더 자연스러워요. 정보에는 '유출하다'를 더 흔하게 써요.
explain_en: With 누출하다, the subject is whoever let the gas or information out. To talk about the result of something seeping out, 누출되다 is more natural. For information, 유출하다 is more common.

examples.en: At home I use a desktop, not a laptop.

examples.ko: 데스크톱이 너무 느려서 새로 사고 싶어요.
examples.en: My desktop is too slow, so I want to buy a new one.
The desktop at the office has a big screen.
I play games on a high-performance desktop.
A desktop is hard to carry around.
I got a desktop that a friend used to use, at a low price.

explain: '데스크톱'은 책상 위에 두고 쓰는 컴퓨터예요. 표준 표기는 '데스크톱'이지만 '데스크탑'이라고 쓰는 사람도 많아요. 들고 다니는 컴퓨터는 '노트북'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: 데스크톱 is a computer you keep on a desk. The standard spelling is 데스크톱, but many people write 데스크탑. A computer you carry around is called 노트북.

en: drawing; blueprint; plan (of a building or machine)

examples.en: The architect drew the plans for the new house.

examples.ko: 이 도면이 있으면 방이 몇 개인지 바로 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: With this plan, you can tell right away how many rooms there are.
The factory made the parts exactly as the machine drawing shows.

examples.ko: 도면 한 장이 없어서 공사가 늦어졌어요.
examples.en: One drawing was missing, so the construction was delayed.

examples.ko: 이사 가기 전에 집 도면을 받아 봤어요.
examples.en: Before moving, I received the plan of the house.

examples.ko: 도면에 문제가 있어서 다시 확인해야 해요.
examples.en: There is a problem with the drawing, so we have to check again.

explain: '도면'은 집이나 기계를 만들기 전에 보는 설계 그림이라서 공사와 공장 이야기에 많이 나와요. 방 구조만 간단히 그린 건 '평면도'라고 해요. 보통 그림은 '그림'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 도면 is the design drawing used before building a house or machine, so it comes up in talk about construction and factories. A simple drawing of just the room layout is a 평면도. An ordinary picture is a 그림.

examples.ko: 역사책에서 마을 사람들의 몰살 이야기를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read a story about the massacre of a village in a history book.

examples.ko: 그 전쟁은 한 민족의 몰살로 이어졌어요.
examples.en: That war led to the wiping out of a people.

examples.ko: 영화 속에서 병사들이 몰살 직전까지 갔어요.
examples.en: In the movie, the soldiers came close to being wiped out.
People ran away to avoid being slaughtered.

examples.ko: 공룡의 몰살은 큰 운석 때문이라고 해요.
examples.en: They say the dinosaurs' wiping out was caused by a huge meteorite.
A terrible massacre happens in this story.

explain: '몰살'은 한 사람이 아니라 한 무리가 통째로 죽는 큰 사건에 써요. '전멸'은 군대나 팀이 모두 없어지는 것이라, 게임에서 팀이 다 죽어도 '전멸했다'고 말해요. 실제 사건을 말할 땐 무거운 말이에요.
explain_en: 몰살 is for a big event in which a whole group dies, not just one person. 전멸 is when an army or team is entirely lost, and in games a team that all dies can be said to be 전멸했다. For real events, 몰살 is a heavy word.

examples.en: The enemy army massacred the villagers.
In the movie, a monster wipes out the people.

examples.ko: 게임 속 몬스터를 몰살해서 점수를 얻었어요.
examples.en: I wiped out the monsters in the game and earned points.
The plan to wipe them out became known.

examples.ko: 농장 주인은 병든 닭을 몰살해야 했어요.
examples.en: The farm owner had to cull all the sick chickens.

examples.ko: 모기를 몰살하고 나니 잠이 잘 와요.
examples.en: After wiping out the mosquitoes, I can sleep well.

explain: '몰살하다'의 목적어는 사람 무리나 동물 떼예요. 게임이나 모기 같은 가벼운 상황에서도 쓰지만, 실제 사건에서는 아주 무거운 말이에요. 당한 쪽에서 말할 때는 '몰살당하다'를 써요.
explain_en: The object of 몰살하다 is a group of people or a swarm of animals. It is used lightly with games or mosquitoes, but for real events it is a very heavy word. From the victims' side, you say 몰살당하다.

examples.ko: 경찰은 사망 원인을 알려고 부검을 했어요.
examples.en: The police performed an autopsy to learn the cause of death.

examples.ko: 부검 결과가 다음 주에 나올 거예요.
examples.en: The autopsy results will come out next week.
The family did not agree to an autopsy.
I watched a drama with an autopsy scene.
The case was solved only after the autopsy was done.

examples.ko: 부검 없이는 정확한 원인을 알기 어려워요.
examples.en: Without an autopsy, it is hard to know the exact cause.

explain: '부검'은 죽음의 원인이 확실하지 않을 때 하는 일이라서 뉴스와 드라마에 자주 나와요. 병원에서 살아 있는 사람의 몸을 보는 건 '검사'라고 해요.
explain_en: 부검 is done when the cause of death is unclear, so it shows up often in news and dramas. Examining the body of a living person at a hospital is called 검사.

examples.en: The doctors are performing an autopsy on the body.
The police performed an autopsy on the deceased yesterday.
To find the cause, an autopsy has to be done.
The family waited outside while the autopsy was going on.

examples.ko: 동물을 부검하고 나서 병의 이유를 알았어요.
examples.en: After the animal was autopsied, we learned the reason for the illness.
I heard the autopsy will be done tomorrow.

explain: '부검하다' 앞에는 '시신을', '사망자를'이 오고, 가끔 '동물을'도 와요. '부검을 하다'라고 풀어 말해도 같아요.
explain_en: Before 부검하다 you usually find '시신을' or '사망자를', and sometimes '동물을'. You can also split it into '부검을 하다' with the same meaning.

en: be scattered about; be dotted around

examples.ko: 작은 섬들이 바다 위에 산재해 있어요.
examples.en: Small islands are scattered across the sea.

examples.ko: 공원에는 쓰레기가 산재해서 보기 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Trash is strewn around the park, so it looks bad.

examples.ko: 이 지역에는 오래된 절이 곳곳에 산재해요.
examples.en: Old temples are scattered throughout this region.

examples.ko: 문제가 산재한 회사라서 고칠 게 많아요.
examples.en: The company has problems all over, so there is a lot to fix.

examples.ko: 자료가 여러 파일에 산재할 때는 정리가 필요해요.
examples.en: When data is scattered across many files, it needs to be organized.
Toys were scattered all over the child's room.

explain: '산재하다'는 물건·건물·문제가 여기저기 흩어져 있을 때 써요. 보통 '산재해 있다' 모양으로 말해요. 한곳에 모여 있으면 '밀집하다'를 쓰고, 일상에서는 '흩어져 있다'가 더 쉬워요.
explain_en: 산재하다 is for objects, buildings, or problems spread out here and there. It usually appears as 산재해 있다. Things packed in one place are 밀집하다, and in daily talk 흩어져 있다 is easier.

examples.ko: 이 과자에는 인공 색소가 들어 있지 않아요.
examples.en: This snack contains no artificial coloring.
Carrots turn orange because of their pigment.

examples.ko: 피부는 색소에 따라 색이 달라 보여요.
examples.en: Skin looks different in color depending on the pigment.
I added coloring to make the cake pink.

examples.ko: 옷에 묻은 색소는 쉽게 지워지지 않아요.
examples.en: Dye that gets on clothes doesn't come out easily.

examples.ko: 식용 색소는 조금만 써도 색이 진해요.
examples.en: Even a little food coloring makes the color deep.

explain: 과자 겉면에 '합성 색소'라고 쓰여 있으면 인공으로 색을 낸 거예요. 자연에서 얻은 건 '천연 색소'라고 해요. 그림을 그리는 건 '물감', 머리를 물들이는 건 '염색약'이라고 따로 불러요.
explain_en: If a snack label says '합성 색소', the color is artificial; one from nature is a '천연 색소'. Paint for drawing is 물감, and hair dye is called 염색약, so they have separate words.

examples.en: Because of his faith, he became a martyr.
This cathedral was built to remember the martyrs.
I read a martyr's story in a book.

examples.ko: 이 산에서 수백 명의 순교자가 나왔어요.
examples.en: Hundreds of martyrs came from this mountain.

examples.ko: 그 사람을 순교자처럼 생각하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people think of that person as a martyr.
On Martyrs' Day, people gather to pray.

explain: '순교자'는 믿음 때문에 목숨을 잃은 사람이라서 종교 이야기에 써요. 나라를 위해 목숨을 바친 사람은 '순국선열'이나 '열사'라고 불러요. 어떤 일에 크게 희생한 사람을 비유로 '순교자'라고 하기도 해요.
explain_en: 순교자 is someone who lost their life for their faith, so it belongs to religious topics. A person who gave their life for the country is called 순국선열 or 열사. It is also used figuratively for someone who sacrificed a lot for a cause.

en: how bad it must be (rhetorical); how desperate one must be

examples.en: How bad must it have been for that person to quit the company?
How bad must it have been that I couldn't even tell Mom?
How desperate must that child have been to tell a lie?
Do you think I would ask like this if it weren't so serious?
It must have been serious for a friend to come all the way to my house.

examples.ko: 추운 날 밖에서 일하는 사람은 오죽하겠어요.
examples.en: Imagine how hard it is for people who work outside on a cold day.

explain: '오죽하면 ~겠어요?', '오죽했으면 ~을까요?', '오죽하겠어요?'처럼 물음 꼴로 써요. '얼마나 힘들었으면 그랬겠어요'라는 공감의 말이에요. 대답을 바라는 질문이 아니고, 그 사람의 행동이나 처지를 이해해 줄 때 써요.
explain_en: It is used in question forms such as '오죽하면 ~겠어요?', '오죽했으면 ~을까요?', and '오죽하겠어요?', showing sympathy: 'it must have been that hard for them.' It expects no answer; you use it to show you understand someone's action or situation.

en: the original judgment (the lower court's ruling under appeal)

examples.en: The appeals court upheld the original ruling as it was.
The lawyer said the original sentence was too heavy.
Everyone was surprised because the original verdict was changed.

examples.ko: 그 사건은 원심과 같은 결과로 끝났어요.
examples.en: The case ended with the same result as the original ruling.
In the original trial it was not guilty, but now it has changed.

examples.ko: 원심은 유죄라고 봤지만 대법원은 다르게 판단했어요.
examples.en: The original court found guilt, but the Supreme Court judged differently.

explain: '원심'은 윗 법원이 다시 살펴볼 때 그 바로 앞 재판의 판결을 가리키는 법원 말이에요. 뉴스에서는 '원심 유지', '원심 파기'로 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: 원심 refers to the judgment of the trial just before, when a higher court reviews it; it is a court term. The news often says '원심 유지' or '원심 파기'. You hardly ever use it in daily conversation.

examples.en: Hmm, I'll have to think about that.

examples.ko: 으음, 맛이 좀 이상한 것 같아요.
examples.en: Hmm, the taste seems a little strange.
Mm, that could be so.

examples.ko: 으음, 어디에 뒀는지 기억이 안 나요.
examples.en: Hmm, I can't remember where I put it.
Mm, I'm tired today and want to rest.
Hmm, a good idea just came to me!

explain: '으음'은 대답하기 전에 생각하거나 망설일 때 내는 소리예요. '음'보다 길게 끌어서 더 깊이 고민하는 느낌이 나요. 맞장구칠 때는 '응'이나 '네'를 써요.
explain_en: 으음 is a sound you make while thinking or hesitating before you answer. It is drawn out longer than 음 and sounds like deeper thought. To show you agree, you say 응 or 네.

en: north of (a line or river); the northern part of Korea (North Korea area)

examples.en: My grandmother is someone who came down from the North.

examples.ko: 서울 이북 지역은 눈이 더 많이 와요.
examples.en: The area north of Seoul gets more snow.
North of the Han River, there are many old markets.
I heard a northern dialect from the North for the first time.
Naengmyeon is known as a food from the North.

examples.ko: 휴전선 이북은 일반인이 갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: Ordinary people can't go north of the armistice line.

explain: '이북'은 어떤 기준선의 위쪽을 말해요. '한강 이북'처럼 쓰고, 아래쪽은 '이남'이에요. 그냥 '이북'이라고만 하면 분단 때 북쪽에 있던 지역을 가리키기도 해요. 지금 나라를 말할 때는 '북한'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 이북 means the area above a certain line, as in '한강 이북', and the area below is 이남. Used alone, it can also refer to the region that was in the north at the time of the division. For the country today, say 북한.

examples.ko: 권한 이양은 다음 달에 이루어질 거예요.
examples.en: The transfer of authority will take place next month.
The president promised to hand over power.

examples.ko: 업무 이양 때문에 요즘 회의가 많아요.
examples.en: There are many meetings these days because of the handover of work.

examples.ko: 이양 절차가 끝나서 새 팀장이 일을 시작했어요.
examples.en: The handover procedure ended, and the new team leader started working.

examples.ko: 지방에 대한 권한 이양이 논의되고 있어요.
examples.en: Handing authority over to the regions is being discussed.

examples.ko: 정권 이양 뒤에도 정책은 크게 안 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: Even after the transfer of power, policy didn't change much.

explain: '이양'은 권한·권력·업무를 다른 사람이나 기관에 넘길 때 써요. 물건을 건네는 건 '전달', 일을 맡기는 건 '위임'이에요. '이양'은 넘긴 사람이 손을 떼는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: 이양 is for passing authority, power, or work to another person or body. Handing over an object is 전달, and entrusting a task is 위임. 이양 carries the sense that the one who hands it over steps away.

examples.en: The company hands authority over to team leaders.
The CEO handed over management rights last month.
I will hand the work over to the new employee.
After handing over the responsibility, I feel lighter.
The process of handing over power ended peacefully.

examples.ko: 지방 정부에 일을 이양해서 처리가 빨라졌어요.
examples.en: Work was passed to the local government, so processing got faster.

explain: '이양하다' 앞에는 권한·권력·경영권·업무가 와요. 물건이나 돈은 '넘기다'를 쓰고, 책임을 일부만 맡길 때는 '위임하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Before 이양하다 you find authority, power, management rights, or work. For objects or money, use 넘기다, and for entrusting only part of a responsibility, use 위임하다.
